q: 1. A simply supported beam of length l carries a load varying uniformly from zero at left end to maximum at right end. Maximum bending moment occurs at a distance of
explain: For a triangular (0 to max) UDL, the max BM occurs at x = L/√3 measured from the zero-load end.

q: 2. Determinate beam can be analyzed with the help of
explain: A statically determinate beam can be fully solved using the three equations of static equilibrium (ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, ΣM=0).

q: 3. A beam fixed at both ends with a central load W in the middle will have zero bending moment at
explain: A fixed-fixed beam with central point load develops two points of contraflexure (zero BM), symmetric about mid-span.

q: 4. The maximum bending moment caused on a simply supported beam subjected to two equal concentrated loads (W/2) spaced at equal distance (L/3) over the span is
explain: For this standard two-point-load arrangement at the third-points, max BM = WL/6.

q: 5. A beam is said to be of uniform strength if
options: bending moment is same throughout the beam
deflection is same throughout the beam
bending stress is same throughout the beam
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: the classic textbook definition of 'uniform strength' is usually stated as constant bending stress throughout — worth double-checking against your source book if this seems inconsistent).

q: 6. A section of a beam is said to be in pure bending if it is subjected to
options: constant bending moment and constant shear force
constant bending moment and zero shear force
constant shear force and zero bending moment
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook definition of pure bending is constant BM with zero shear force — worth double-checking against your source book, as this may be a possible key erratum).

q: 7. The maximum deflection of a beam occurs at
explain: Maximum deflection occurs where the slope of the elastic curve (dy/dx) is zero.

q: 8. The slope of an elastic curve at the point of contraflexure
explain: At a contraflexure point, only BM=0 is guaranteed; the slope can take any value there.

q: 9. If the length of a simply supported beam carrying a concentrated load at the centre is doubled, the deflection at the center will become
explain: Since δ ∝ L³, doubling the span increases deflection by a factor of 2³ = 8.

q: 10. The maximum deflection in a cantilever beam carrying a concentrated load 'w' at the free end
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/3EI for a cantilever with a point load at the free end.

q: 11. The maximum deflection in a cantilever beam carrying uniformly distributed load (w) over its span
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = WL³/8EI for a cantilever under UDL (W = total load = wL).

q: 12. The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam subjected to uniformly distributed load (w) over the span is
explain: Standard formula: δ_max = 5WL³/384EI for UDL on a simply supported beam (W = total load = wL).

q: 13. The diagram showing the variation of BM along the span of a beam is called
explain: By definition, a Bending Moment Diagram (BMD) plots BM variation along the span. (Double-check this against your printed key — some editions mismark this answer.)

q: 14. A diagram which shows the variation of axial force is called
explain: A thrust diagram plots the variation of axial (normal) force along a member.

q: 15. A beam of uniform strength will have at every cross-section the same
explain: A beam of uniform strength is designed so bending stress remains constant at every section, by varying the section dimensions.

q: 16. In a beam, the neutral plane
options: passes through the c.g. of the area of c/s
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook fact is that the neutral axis passes through the centroid of the cross-section — worth double-checking against your source book).

q: 17. Longitudinal cracks observed in timber beams are due to
options: application of concentrated loads over the beam
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: longitudinal splitting along the grain in timber is classically attributed to horizontal shear failure between layers — worth double-checking against your source book).

q: 18. The expression EI d⁴y/dx⁴ at any section for a beam is equal to
explain: Differentiating the beam equation twice more: EI·d⁴y/dx⁴ = w, the load intensity.

q: 19. The slope of curve of B.M. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of loading at that section
the slope of shear force diagram at that section
the ordinate of shear force diagram at that section
the area of shear force diagram starting from any one end
explain: Since dM/dx = V, the slope of the BM curve at any point equals the SF value (ordinate) there.

q: 20. The slope of curve of S.F. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of loading at that section
the ordinate of loading diagram at that section
the area of loading diagram from end to that section
the bending moment at that section
explain: Since dV/dx = -w, the slope of the SF curve equals the load intensity ordinate at that section.

q: 21. The difference between BM values at any two sections will be equal to
options: the area of SF diagram between those two sections
the area of loading diagram between the two sections
the area of bending moment between the two sections
explain: ΔM between two sections equals the area under the shear force diagram between them (∫V dx).

q: 22. The difference between SF values at any two sections will be equal to
options: the area of bending moment between the two sections
the difference between the slopes of the curve of loading diagram at two sections
the ordinate of shear force diagram at one section plus the slope of the loading diagram multiplied by the distance between two sections
the area of the loading diagram between those two sections
explain: ΔV between two sections equals the area under the load intensity diagram between them (∫w dx).

q: 23. The bending moment in a cable carrying a system of loads will be
explain: A flexible cable carries load purely by axial tension along its curved shape — it develops no bending moment anywhere.

q: 24. The number of points of contraflexure in a simply supported beam carrying UDL, is
explain: A simply supported beam under UDL sags throughout its span, so BM never changes sign — zero contraflexure points.

q: 25. BM in a cantilever beam having span 1.8m and uniformly distributed load of 4kg/m
26. A point where SF is zero, BM is
explain: Where SF=0, BM reaches a local extremum — this could be either a maximum (sagging peak) or minimum (hogging peak) depending on the loading.

q: 27. The rate of change of shear force is called
explain: dV/dx = -w — the rate of change of shear force equals the load intensity.

q: 28. Find the value of thrust, if the member (beam) is subjected to an inclined force having magnitude 5 kN and inclination with vertical is 30°
explain: Thrust (component along the horizontal beam axis) = 5 × sin30° = 2.5 kN.

q: 29. At the point of application of a concentrated load on a beam, there is
options: sudden change of slope of BM
explain: A point load causes a sudden jump (discontinuity) in the shear force diagram, which produces a sudden change in the slope of the BM diagram at that point.

q: 30. The number of reaction components at a hinge on rollers support is
explain: A roller support provides only one reaction component, perpendicular to the rolling surface.

q: 31. A cantilever beam is the one which is supported with
options: one end hinge and other on rollers
one end fixed and other on rollers
one end fixed and the other free
explain: A cantilever has one fixed end providing full restraint, and a completely free other end.

q: 32. Which of the following end conditions permits the displacement in any direction and also rotation?
explain: A free end has no restraint at all — it permits both translation and rotation.

q: 33. A beam is supported over three rollers lying in the same plane. The beam is stable for
options: loading with no component in the direction of the beam
loading with no component perpendicular to the direction of beam
only when no load except self weight acts
explain: Three rollers alone provide no horizontal restraint and are generally unstable except under special/self-weight-only loading conditions.

q: 34. The beam strongest in flexure will have maximum
explain: Bending strength (moment capacity) is governed by section modulus Z = I/y_max, not I alone.

q: 35. Moment of inertia of a rectangular beam b×d is
explain: Standard formula: I = bd³/12 about the centroidal axis parallel to b, with d as the depth.

q: 36. The ratio of moment of inertia of a square section to that of a circular section for a given depth is given by
explain: For the same depth (square side = circle diameter), the square section has more material further from the axis, giving I_square/I_circle > 1.

q: 37. The section modulus of a circular section about an axis through its C.G. is
explain: Standard formula: Z = I/y_max = (πd⁴/64)/(d/2) = πd³/32.

q: 38. The shear force in a concrete beam is assumed to act
options: on a plane normal to the longitudinal axis
explain: Transverse shear force acts perpendicular to the beam's longitudinal axis.

q: 39. The shear force on a beam is proportional to
explain: Shear force at a section equals the algebraic sum of all transverse forces on one side of that section.

q: 40. Rate of change of bending moment is equal to
explain: dM/dx = V — the fundamental beam relation between bending moment and shear force.

q: 41. The rate of change of shear force is called
explain: dV/dx = -w — the rate of change of shear force equals (negative) load intensity.

q: 42. The amount of shear force at the maximum bending moment is
explain: Since dM/dx = V, bending moment is maximum where shear force is zero (i.e. minimum).

q: 43. In case of a simply supported beam subjected to UDL the maximum shear force occurs at a point
explain: For UDL on a simply supported beam, shear force is maximum at the supports and zero at mid-span.

q: 44. Shear force diagram for a cantilever carrying a UDL over its whole length is
explain: SF varies linearly from zero at the free end to wL at the fixed end — a triangle.

q: 45. The difference in ordinate of the shear force between any two sections is equal to the area under
options: shear curve between these two sections
load curve between these two sections
bending moment curve between these two sections
load curve between these two sections plus concentrated load applied between the sections
explain: ΔV between two sections = area under the load intensity diagram between them.

q: 46. In an I section almost all the shear force is taken by
explain: The web carries the vast majority (~90%+) of the transverse shear force in an I-section.

q: 47. A Prismatic bar when subjected to pure bending assumes the shape of
explain: Under pure (constant) bending moment, a prismatic bar bends into a circular arc of constant curvature.

q: 48. If a constant section is subjected to a uniform/pure bending moment throughout, its length bends to
explain: Constant bending moment produces constant curvature — hence a circular arc.

q: 49. A shear force diagram of a simply supported beam shows constant shear force throughout the span. It is subjected to
options: two concentrated loads spaced at points
explain: A pure applied couple (no other transverse loads) produces a constant shear force with a jump in the moment diagram, but constant SF throughout.

q: 50. The shear force on a beam and the displacement are related by
explain: As per the answer key; the standard beam relation is V = EI·d³y/dx³ (third derivative of deflection).
